title: tenant-safe hotpatcher for data-plane with stateful health gating
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: On VPC/private deployments we still see customer-facing errors and cold-start latency spikes during rolling upgrades of the inference data plane. Current draining is purely pod-level and doesn't account for model KV cache priming, long-lived websocket connections, or tenant affinity. We need an automated upgrade mechanism that 'hotpatches' nodes without inducing 5xxs or large latency tails, and that can reliably rollback when metrics cross safety thresholds.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware hotpatcher operator and supporting Terraform/IaC knobs to: (1) gate progress on stateful health signals (primed KV cache, active connection handoff), (2) align drain windows with cache TTLs, (3) run safe canaries at tenant/granularity, and (4) provide deterministic automatic rollback and audit trail for Private/VPC runtime upgrades.
acceptance_criteria:
- Upgrades proceed with zero customer 5xx regressions in canary tenants during 95% of runs in staging.
- For each upgrade, operator can report a safety_quorum metric and refuses to shift >10% traffic if priming <75% across nodes.
- Terraform module exposes parameters: upgrade_strategy (hotpatch|recreate|drain-only), drain_grace_seconds, priming_timeout_seconds, safety_quorum_pct.
- Rollback triggers automatically when SLO breach or circuit-breaker threshold reached and is logged in audit trails (Confluence runbook + console event).
- Smoke tests (load + embeddings) pass for canary tenants before global shift.
- Runbook written and validated with SEs and on-call team.
plan_steps: Design operator: hotpatch controller that orchestrates in-place binary/agent updates without pod restarts where possible (use socket handoff + ephemeral sidecar).
Add stateful health probes: primed_cache_ready, connection_handoff_ready, tenant_session_count, model_kernel_warm.
Extend Terraform module 'private_data_plane' with upgrade knobs and outputs (upgrade_channel, drain_annotation_ttl, safety_quorum_pct).
Implement canary flow: select tenant cohort, run priming phase, run traffic shift window, observe metrics, promote or rollback.
Integrate with console: show per-tenant upgrade status, safety_quorum, priming progress, and a single-click rollback.
Add audit metadata to etcd and S3: upgrade_id, operator_version, inputs, and final outcome.
Create automated rollback policy: immediate rollback on >1% error rate increase over baseline for 5m OR >25% latency P95 regressions for canary tenants.
Implement e2e staging tests and chaos tests (network partition + node OOM) to validate safety net.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for operator reconciliation logic and Terraform module plan.
- Staging: run 10 controlled upgrades across 3 cluster sizes with canary tenants; collect SLO deltas.
- Regression: simulate slow priming and ensure operator extends drain window up to priming_timeout_seconds.
- Chaos: kill primed node during handoff and verify rollback triggers and recovery completes within SLA.
- Performance: measure P50/P95/P99 tokens/sec during hotpatch vs baseline.
- Post-upgrade validation: run regression eval prompt-set for 20 sample tenants and compare semantics with pre-upgrade model using Optimize metrics.
monitoring:
Metrics to add: upgrade_progress_percent, primed_nodes_pct, safety_quorum_pct, canary_error_rate, canary_latency_p95, rollback_count, upgrade_duration_seconds.
Dashboards: private-upgrades (per-cluster, per-tenant), alert rules for canary_error_rate > threshold, and a 'stuck-priming' alert when primed_nodes_pct doesn't change for 10m.
Logs/Tracing: correlate operator events with runtime traces (request_id, upgrade_id) and surface in console traces tab.
rollback_plan:
- Automated rollback triggers: canary_error_rate spike, priming failures, operator health failure, or manual abort by on-call.
- Rollback steps: stop traffic shift, mark new revision as drained, re-instate previous variant in routing, re-prime cache if necessary, and clean up partial artifacts.
- Safety net: use a 'rollback_quarantine' annotation so operator won’t reattempt the same image until a manual review is completed.
- Post-rollback: create a postmortem ticket if rollback_count > 1 for same release and attach logs/metrics to the ticket.
